problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}-3y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $6$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that all the sine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Solving Second Order ODEs Given the Fourier Series of the Forcing Function
examples.problem:
Find the Fourier series of a particular solution of the differential equation $y''-y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $2$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x) \sim 1 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^3\pi} \sin(n\pi x).
$$

*Hint: We may assume that all the cosine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*
examples.worked_solution:
Because the forcing function has only a constant term and sine terms, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
y_p \sim \dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n \sin(n\pi x).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for $y''_p$ and $y_p$ into the equation and have

$$
\sum_{n=1}^\infty -b_n n^2\pi^2 \sin(n\pi x)
-
\left( \dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n \sin(n\pi x) \right)
=
1 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^3\pi} \sin(n\pi x).
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get

$$
-\dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n(-n^2\pi^2-1)\sin(n\pi x)
=
1 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^3\pi} \sin(n\pi x).
$$

Now, equating the free terms and sine coefficients, we obtain:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14074986/assets/249067c54bdeee50fdddb787db0d9fc6e95eeddd7cbf322cb425c08a2a25d97c.png)

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
y_p \sim 
-1
+ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \:
\dfrac{(-1)^n}{n^3\pi(n^2\pi^2+1)}
\cdot
\sin(n\pi x).
$$

feedback.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{′}+5y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $2$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Now, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)) \\  & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\cdot (-n\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))+{b}_{n}\cdot n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x) \\  & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{′}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)) \\  & \,+5(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)) \\  & \,\,={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \frac{5{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({b}_{n}n\pi +5{a}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x) \\  & \,\,+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-{a}_{n}n\pi +5{b}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x) \\  & \,\,\,\,={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, equating the free terms and the cosine and sine coefficients, we obtain the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{5{a}_{0}}{2}=0 \\ {b}_{n}n\pi +5{a}_{n}=0 \\ -{a}_{n}n\pi +5{b}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

Next, from the second equation, 

$$
{a}_{n}=-\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{5}.
$$

Substituting this into the third equation gives

$$
-(-\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{5})n\pi +5{b}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\,⇒\,{b}_{n}=\frac{5(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+25)}
$$

Therefore, for ${a}_{n}$ with $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{5} \\  & =-\frac{n\pi }{5}\cdot \frac{5(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+25)} \\  & =-\frac{(-1)^{n}}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+25)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{(-1)^{n}}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+25)}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+\frac{5(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+25)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$
